items.note: Read CVDR746130/1 (Geldend van 01-01-2026 t/m heden). Voted in the council meeting of 27 October 2025; art. 15 in force 1 January 2026. Tariff table: area A 3.85 and area B 3.45 per hour 09.00-19.00; 19.00-23.00 only a 3.85 figure in the area A column (none for B). Matches. The ordinance does not say which hours the tariff is charged on which days, so the item wording (charged 09:00 to 19:00) rests only on the table headings.

Same CVDR746130/1 tariff table: resident permit one zone 268 (A) and 84 (B); business permit two zones 745 (A) and 185 (B); resident permit with guaranteed space (bracket or barrier) 576 (A only); passe-partout 1,107 per year or 92 per month, in the area A column (B column empty). All numbers match.

Document is the council proposal submitted 6 September 2023 to adopt 'Parkeervisie Enschede: Leefbaar, Aantrekkelijk en Bereikbaar'; builds on the 2012 vision 'Parkeren in Balans' and the March 2020 mobility vision; says capacity problems exist ('Die tijd ligt inmiddels achter ons') and much public space is used for parking. Item correctly words it as a proposal. The title 'Parkeervisie 2023-2030' is not in this document; it appears in the 1 October 2024 tariff proposal (item 11 source), which also says the vision was adopted 'vorig jaar' (2023). Adoption is therefore shown only indirectly, by that later document, not by a decision text.

Page 2: evening tariff of 1 euro per hour from 19.00 in garages, paid street parking extended to 23.00, street tariff 50 cents above garage growing stepwise to 1 euro, regular street tariff 3.30 euros per hour in 2023. All as written and worded as a proposal. Whether the 1 euro garage evening tariff is in force is not shown here.

Page 2-3: no new parking permits in the inner city, only garage subscriptions; blue zones become green zones (register plate, free for a set time depending on location, then regular street tariff); full digitisation and the aim ('Streven') to move to digital enforcement in 2026, with a scan car as the means. Matches; the '2026' attaches to digital enforcement.
Page 1 and 3: garage tariffs set by the college, street tariffs by the council (Wet Markt en Overheid); draft vision shared with Q-Park, whose vision is in line; 440 survey responses. All match.

Page 2: new parking garage near the station and research into P+R at Oldenzaalsestraat and Westerval are listed as proposed measures; page 3 says a garage would be put to the council as a separate proposal. Item correctly says these were proposals.

Council proposal for 14 May 2024: credit 1,116,000 euros = 366,000 for the underground car park study at the bus station + 750,000 for the station bicycle store (up to 650,000 co-financing for the ProRail study plus 100,000 own staff time). Of a 17.8 million national housing grant (SPUK), about 3 million is attributed to the F35, leaving 14.8 million for car park and bus station; the grant condition is that spending is finished in 2035. Item words it as a request to the council (correct); the proposal itself does not show the vote, but the 2025-2028 budget text (item 16) lists the feasibility study as an investment.

Proposal page 1: about 800 homes built in ten years, 1,750 more planned; page 3: dynamic parking balance of April 2022 by Spark shows a new garage is necessary in 2025-2030 as street spaces are removed. Matches.

The document is a B&W (executive) agenda form for the meeting of 11 July 2023 with a concept decision; the 'B&W besluit dd.' line is blank, signing was only planned for 14 July 2023. So 'the executive agreed' is too strong. Supported details: the agreement concerns firms on the Business & Sciencepark applying for building/other-use permits; free car parks around the Grolsch Veste (bijna 900 spaces), free for all except on FC Twente home match days; period of 3 to 5 years (it is the period of the agreement, not specifically of monitoring); no parking charge there for now; VONK and the city monitor the effects; firms more than 800 m walking distance away must add a mobility plan to the permit application.
items.corrected_text: A B&W (executive) agenda form for 11 July 2023 proposed that the executive approve an agreement with the Kennispark business association VONK, for a period of 3 to 5 years, under which firms on the Business & Sciencepark with building or other-use plans may meet extra parking demand at the free car parks around the Grolsch Veste (almost 900 spaces). The form says the city would not introduce a parking charge there for now and that the city and VONK would monitor the effects. Firms more than 800 metres' walk from those car parks would have to attach a mobility plan to their permit application. The form is a proposal: its decision line is blank in the copy read, and signing was planned for 14 July 2023.

items.note: Read both Q-Park pages on 21 October 2026. P+R Parkweg page (the item's source_url): Parkweg t.o. 37-39, 156 spaces (also in page data totalSpots 156), open Monday-Sunday 24-7, tariffs 'konden helaas niet geladen worden', traveller-discount rule (domestic train journey, check in and out at different stations, leave the P+R the same day as the return train trip), nearby list P+R Station (Gieskesstraat), De Brink (Brink 118), 'Zuidmolenstraat 1'. The Zuidmolenstraat figures are NOT on the source_url page but on the separate page https://www.q-park.nl/nl-nl/parkeren/enschede/enschede/ (I read it): 466 spaces, 3 disabled spaces, 4 charging points, 2.00 m height, Kentekenherkenning, 24-7, tariffs did not load. All claims confirmed; add that second URL as a source. The 156 is Q-Park's listed capacity; the 145 measured by our own counts is a different kind of figure and should not be mixed with it. Live page, date 2026-10 and read-on wording are correct.

Council proposal for 1 October 2024: street tariff 3.80 (zone 1 and 1B, +0.05) and 3.40 (zones 2-8, +0.10) for 2025, permit tariffs indexed 2.2 percent, introduction of a tariff for a second resident permit; says 'in de garages een tarief van 3,30 gaat gelden' and keeps a 50 cent gap in zone 1. Worded as a proposal, which is right: the proposal does not show the vote. (The 2026 ordinance art. 14 refers to a 'Verordening Parkeerbelastingen 2025 van 11 november 2024', so a 2025 ordinance exists, but its tariffs are not shown in the sources read.)

Proposal page 1: Parkeerbedrijf Enschede manages and operates paid parking on street and in garages; garage and P+R tariffs set by the college (private-law character); street tariffs by the council. But the Van Heek sentence is garbled: the proposal says the starting points underlie the operating calculation 'inclusief o.a. de afschrijvingen voor de bouw van de H.J. van Heekgarage en de gemeentelijke investering van ruim 20 miljoen euro vanaf 2016 ten behoeve van de aanpassing van deze garage voor het MST', i.e. depreciation for building the garage plus a separate municipal investment of over 20 million euros since 2016 to adapt the garage for the MST hospital; it does not say the garage was built with that 20 million.
items.corrected_text: The same proposal says the municipal Parkeerbedrijf Enschede manages and operates the paid parking on street and in garages, that garage and P+R tariffs are set by the college because of their private-law character, and that street tariffs are set by the council. Its operating calculation includes depreciation for the construction of the H.J. van Heekgarage and a municipal investment of over 20 million euros since 2016 to adapt that garage for the MST hospital.

items.note: Memo of 28 September 2023 to the council. It says 'Met de huidige 3,20 overdag en voorgestelde 1,00 in de avond' the garage budget balances; the 1.00 evening tariff is therefore PROPOSED, not an existing 2023 tariff (the table is headed 'Nieuwe tarieven 2023' and lists garage 3.20 day / 1.00 evening). Visitor permit digital with hours limit via an app: supported. 'No plans to remove pay machines, but the plate must be entered at the machine': supported. The garage budget balancing under the Wet Markt en Overheid at these levels: supported.
items.corrected_text: A memo to the council dated 28 September 2023 says that with the then-current garage day tariff of 3.20 euros and a proposed evening tariff of 1.00 euro the garage budget balances under the Wet Markt en Overheid. It also says visitor permits are to get an hours limit and become digital (via an app), and that there are no plans to remove the pay machines, but drivers would have to enter the plate there.

items.note: Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 306560, published 26 June 2026: college decision on 'Aldus vastgesteld in de vergadering van 23 juni 2026' (based on a proposal of 23 June 2026), in force the day after publication; Exploitant = Gemeente Enschede; art. 4 tariffs published on boards, digital screens at the entrance and/or the municipal parking app or www.enschede.nl/parkeren; art. 5 max 5.00 m long, 2.20 m wide, 2,800 kg, and the posted maximum height; Parkeerbewijs includes kentekenregistratie and QR-code. All match. The document contains no tariffs. enschede.nl itself returned 429 and was not read (not worked around).

Colofon: 'Datum 13-10-2022'. Samenvatting: about 300 public charging points now (May 2022), about 1,000 needed in 2025, 1,500 in 2030, 3,100 in 2035 (doc uses 'laadpalen' in the summary and 'laadpunten' elsewhere); preference for the concession model with the provinces of Gelderland and Overijssel; works towards a zero-emission logistics zone in the centre area. All match. (A 28 Sep 2023 memo says the council adopted the vision on 12 December 2022; the item correctly dates the document itself.)

Live page, undated, read on 21 October 2026 (the text speaks of December 2024 decisions in the future tense, so it is the draft/proposed budget text; the 2024-11 date is not on the page). Page confirms: investment 'Parkeergebouw: Krediet is voor realisatie van een parkeergebouw op het Kennispark. Project vertraagd in afwachting van ontwikkeling Next Twente'; investment 'Stationskwartier: ... haalbaarheidsonderzoek naar een nieuwe ondergrondse parkeergarage en fietsenstalling in het Centrumkwadraat'; maintenance provision for car parks and bicycle stores with a budgeted balance of 3.6 million euros at 1-1-2025. 'Is funded' goes beyond the page, which only lists it as an investment; and the provision covers garages and bicycle stores.
items.corrected_text: The municipal budget 2025-2028 (paragraphs chapter, read as a live page on 21 October 2026) lists a credit for a car park building at Kennispark as delayed pending the Next Twente development, and an investment for a feasibility study into a new underground car park and bicycle store in Centrumkwadraat (the station area). It gives the maintenance provision for car parks and bicycle stores a budgeted balance of 3.6 million euros at 1 January 2025.

items.note: UT Sustainable Mobility Plan, colofon date 18 June 2021: all car drivers get free parking, around 2,551 car spaces; 37 permit-holder spaces; 31 charging stations (2020), 0.25 euro per kWh; testing parking sensors and loops; paid parking mentioned as an intervention at most universities. All match. Figures are from 2020-2021.

corrected_summary: Enschede's council voted the Verordening Parkeerbelastingen 2026 on 27 October 2025, in force from 1 January 2026: on-street parking costs 3.85 euros an hour in tariff area A and 3.45 euros in area B from 09:00 to 19:00, with area A also charging 3.85 euros from 19:00 to 23:00. Annual resident permits cost 268 euros in area A and 84 euros in area B. The Parkeervisie (later called Parkeervisie 2023-2030 in a 2024 council proposal, which says it was adopted in 2023) was proposed to the council in September 2023: it steers drivers from the street into garages by keeping the street tariff above the garage tariff, proposed no new street permits in the inner city, turning blue zones into green zones and digital enforcement from 2026; a 1 euro evening garage tariff was proposed then, but this research did not confirm it is in force. For 2025 a council proposal of October 2024 suggested 3.80 and 3.40 euros an hour on the street (the final 2025 figures were not read). The municipality's Parkeerbedrijf operates the municipal garages, and general garage conditions were decided by the college on 23 June 2026 and published on 26 June 2026. Q-Park lists a 466-space garage at Zuidmolenstraat 1 and the P+R Parkweg with 156 spaces (page read on 21 October 2026). A May 2024 council proposal asked for a 1.116 million euro credit for feasibility studies, 366,000 euros for an underground car park at the bus station and 750,000 euros for a station bicycle store, and says 14.8 million euros of a national housing grant remain for the car park and bus station, to be spent by 2035; the council vote is not shown, but the budget text lists the study as an investment, and a car park at Kennispark is described there as delayed. A July 2023 executive agenda form proposed letting Kennispark firms use the free car parks around the Grolsch Veste (almost 900 spaces) for 3 to 5 years. The University of Twente reported about 2,551 free campus spaces in its 2021 plan, and the city's 2022 charging vision counted about 300 public charge points against a need of about 1,000 for 2025.
